project.name: Wakil Ahmed Marketplace Seller Portal
project.description: Build a secure, production-ready seller account and vendor management system for Wakil Ahmed Marketplace.

database.connection: Use the database connection string from Render environment variables. Never hardcode credentials.

primary_goal: Create a working seller registration, secure login, seller dashboard, and administrator dashboard connected to the existing backend, PostgreSQL database, Render service, and Shopify store.

seller_accounts: Seller registration with name, email, phone, and password
Admin approval before a seller can publish products
seller_dashboard: Product creation, editing, and submission for approval
Seller order view and order status
admin_dashboard: Review, approve, reject, suspend, and reactivate seller accounts
Review and approve seller product submissions
Manage seller permissions and account status
View seller activity and audit history
shopify_integration: Use Shopify Admin API securely from the backend
Keep API credentials in Render environment variables
Create or update Shopify products only after the required admin approval
Handle Shopify API errors and rate limits safely
Do not place private API credentials in browser code or Shopify theme files

database_requirements.instruction: Inspect the existing PostgreSQL schema and data before making changes. Use safe, reversible migrations.
requirements: Use appropriate primary keys, foreign keys, indexes, and constraints
Store password hashes only, never plain-text passwords
Store token hashes where appropriate and expire verification/reset tokens
Never drop, truncate, or overwrite existing tables or production data without explicit approval

technical_requirements: First inspect the existing GitHub repository, package files, server code, routes, and database schema
Reuse and repair the existing project rather than creating a duplicate application
Use the existing technology stack where practical
Implement server-side validation and authorization for every protected operation
Use secure password hashing, session handling, CSRF protection where applicable, and rate limiting
Protect against SQL injection, XSS, and unauthorized access
Provide clear error messages without exposing secrets or internal stack traces
Create a responsive, accessible interface for desktop and mobile
Add automated tests for registration, login, password reset, seller permissions, and admin approvals
Document setup, environment variables, migrations, and deployment steps

instructions: Connect the existing GitHub repository to the intended Render Web Service
Inspect and preserve the existing service configuration
Configure the existing Render PostgreSQL database using environment variables
Set the correct build and start commands based on the repository
Review deployment logs and resolve build or runtime errors
Verify the deployed application and database connection
render_deployment.secrets_policy: Use placeholders in documentation only. Obtain real values from the appropriate provider and store them in Render environment variables. Never print, commit, or expose secret values.

acceptance_tests: A new seller can register and verify their email
An unapproved seller cannot publish products
An administrator can approve or reject a seller
An approved seller can log in and access only their own dashboard and records
A seller cannot access another seller's products or orders
Password reset works securely and reset links expire
Approved products can be synchronized with Shopify through the backend
The application remains connected to the existing PostgreSQL database after deployment
The production deployment passes health checks and has no unresolved critical errors
strict_instructions: Do not ask the user to change the existing PostgreSQL password as a routine setup step
Do not expose or repeat credentials that may have appeared in chat
Do not commit .env files, passwords, tokens, or private keys to GitHub
Do not put backend server code or database credentials into Shopify theme JSON or Liquid
Do not delete existing repository files, database tables, records, or Render services without explicit approval
Do not publish or deploy untested destructive changes
Explain any required user action in simple, specific steps
delivery_requirements: Render deployment instructions and deployment verification
instruction_to_claude: Start by auditing the existing repository and Render deployment configuration. Report what already works and what is missing. Then implement the system in small, safe steps, test each step, and prepare the Render deployment. Do not claim a feature is complete unless it has been implemented and verified.
